rationale: The literature confirms that hypotonia and seizures can occur in individuals with LRRC7-related neurodevelopmental disorder (e.g., Khan et al. reported a proband with tonic seizures and hypotonia), overturning any assumption that these neurological features are absent. Furthermore, behavioral disturbance (notably aggression and impulsivity) and abnormal eating behaviors (hyperphagia with obesity) are prominent recurrent features in LRRC7 cohorts (Willim et al., Vevera et al.). However, the designation of hyperphagia-associated obesity as an invariant primary discriminator is conflicted by individual clinical presentations presenting with the diametric opposite phenotype (such as failure to thrive in Khan et al.), and hyperphagia/obesity was reported only in a subset ('several cases') rather than across the whole cohort. Additionally, head-to-head discriminator studies against other postsynaptic density scaffold synaptopathies (SYNGAP1, SHANK3, DLG4) are currently qualitative rather than statistically validated clinical diagnostic criteria.

evidence.text: Characterization of 33 individuals with heterozygous LRRC7 variants revealed a core spectrum involving intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, aggressive behavior, and in several individuals, hyperphagia-associated obesity developing in early childhood.

conflicts: While hyperphagia-associated obesity is reported as a distinctive finding in several individuals in the primary LRRC7 cohort (Willim et al., 2024), subsequent cases with de novo variants (Khan et al., 2026) have presented with failure to thrive rather than obesity, showing that abnormal weight trajectory is bidirectional and not universally marked by obesity.

Seizures and hypotonia cannot be considered absent in LRRC7-related disorder; both Khan et al. (2026) and Vevera et al. (2019) note hypotonia and seizures in affected individuals, meaning their presence cannot rule out LRRC7 in favor of SYNGAP1 or SHANK3.
Comparative discriminator accuracy against other PSD synaptopathies (e.g., SYNGAP1, SHANK3, DLG4) remains unquantified by formal sensitivity/specificity analysis in prospective clinical cohorts.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true penetrance and age of onset of hyperphagia and obesity versus failure to thrive across all molecularly confirmed LRRC7 cases?
new_directions.rationale: Understanding whether early failure to thrive routinely transitions to late-onset hyperphagia and obesity (similar to Prader-Willi syndrome) is critical before using hyperphagia as a clinical discriminator in young infants.

new_directions.question_text: How do quantitative behavioral rating scales for aggression and impulsivity compare directly between age-matched cohorts of LRRC7, SYNGAP1, and SHANK3 patients?
new_directions.rationale: Direct comparative phenotyping is required to determine whether the aggressive profile of LRRC7 is quantitatively distinctive or merely overlapping with severe behavioral disruption seen in other postsynaptic density synaptopathies.
